M1: Changes to the actual algorithm, architecture, objective or procedure; renaming and additional explanation alone are not method changes.
E1: Datasets, tasks, domains or test scenarios actually used; changes to splits or sample counts within a task belong to E3.
E2: Comparison methods actually evaluated in the corresponding experiments; a new citation alone does not count.
E3: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, budgets, model sizes or testing procedures; newly disclosed information about existing settings belongs to D1.
E4: Ablations, sensitivity, distribution shifts, error analyses or case studies; identify the actual question tested.
E5: Reporting of repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; changes in numerical values alone belong to E6.
E6: Changes in numerical values, rankings, trends or result entries; different experimental conditions do not establish same-setting performance gains.
T1: Mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, derivations or proofs; equivalent notation and formatting are not theory changes.
C1: Scientific claims and their scope in the abstract, introduction or conclusion; more evidence alone does not establish a changed claim.
C2: Interpretations, mechanisms, applicability boundaries, failure conditions or limitations; distinguish observations from explanations.
D1: Implementation, parameters, hardware, processing and code/data access; distinguish new disclosures from actual changes in settings.
R1: Added or removed citations and changes to positioning relative to prior work; numbering and bibliographic corrections are presentation changes.
P1: Language, terminology, paragraphs, section order and narrative organization; verify scientific changes separately in the relevant dimensions.
P2: Added, removed, redrawn or relocated figures/tables, legends and layout; numerical updates within an otherwise unchanged table belong to E6.
